scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The 1650 opening is a selected colonial phase, not the beginning of Indigenous occupation. The map intervals 1650 to 1715, 1878 to 1914 and 1914 to present do not establish political founding, ending or extinction. Shared regional presentation identifies historical phases rather than one continuous state. No unverified successor links or border claims are added.

The imported Surinam summary concerns the Common Surinam toad. A researched prose override and null summary attribution prevent that unrelated article from appearing. The raw generated source remains intact, and an empty wikipedia override avoids encouraging a future namesake match. Dutch Guiana is interpreted from its actual 1878 polygon, not applied to every historical use of the wider term.

The Jodensavanne conservation report was read through the web PDF reader after direct download encountered a website challenge. Pages 12 and 13 describe excavations of House de Meza and a nearby cooking house. Fieldwork dates are not manufacture dates. Indigenous and Maroon pottery labels are the report’s identifications. Mixed objects support investigation of interaction, not individual ethnicity, equal status or a census of all households. The report’s claims that pipes demonstrate specifically enslaved women smoking are not adopted: pipe fragments alone cannot establish the user’s gender or legal status.

The report’s suggestion that phytolith analysis could illuminate foods is not presented as completed analysis. The gallery captions document recovered plate, jug and cauldron, but give no precise historical date for each object. Captions were read; the card does not claim images or full unpublished excavation records were inspected. The preliminary identification of military post Gelderland and proposed Cassipora boundary changes are excluded.

The sifter is a museum object from Pikin Saron, not a documented excavated artifact. Its 2022 account is distinguished from the 1916 comparison image in the broader Guianas. No population total, fixed ancient origin or incomplete cassava-processing recipe is adopted.

The Smithsonian spoon explanation is explicitly the collective account of Matawai community visitors in 2018. The collection record’s 1968 accession date is not a date of manufacture. No vessel contents were chemically tested, and the account is not assigned to every Maroon community. The relevant full indexed Smithsonian catalogue text was read after direct opening failed.

The bed and samplers represent particular parts of the Surinaams Museum collection, including elite colonial furniture and European women’s needlework. Neither implies common access or a uniform national household. The museum’s unsupported broad archaeological migration and displacement chronology, timeless sustainability language, and stereotyped group descriptions are not used.

Schouten’s 1817 model depicts six enslaved rowers and one steersman; the latter is not assigned a legal status unsupported by the catalogue. Shelter for passengers is not proof of every boat’s design or every passenger’s identity. The model is explicitly an artwork, not a photograph or excavation.

The Milwaukee collection page is used for a specific captioned food stirrer and the distinction between functional and decorative gifts. Broad claims about what all Ndyuka men, women or children do, contemporary clothing, body modification and universal marriage obligations are omitted. The object’s message is not translated by the source and is not invented. The historical label reproduced in the museum text is not adopted as a community name.

Afáka’s development is dated only to the early twentieth century because the consulted encoding proposal gives 1908 while other histories give 1910. No exact invention day, current speaker count, literacy percentage or current encoding status is asserted. The two-stroke and four-stroke sign explanations are from page 1 of the 2012 proposal. No private-use font glyph is embedded as if it were a universally supported character.

The Indian immigration guide is read as an account of registers, not a complete census. The 1873 to 1916 interval concerns direct indentured migration from British India, not all people of Indian origin or the end of every contract. Earlier migration via other colonies is acknowledged by the guide and is not erased. Conflicting headline totals are omitted. Family records are described without accessing or publishing identifiable personal data.

The 2024 volunteer project is a dated example of supervised intergenerational learning. It is separate from the 2023 gallery’s fieldwork. Children’s names are unnecessary and are omitted. The UNESCO co-management description is not evidence that all land or heritage disputes are settled.

The colonial chronology distinguishes capture in 1667, recapture in 1668, British occupations in 1799 to 1802 and 1804 to 1816, and the 1814 agreement from transfer in 1816. Sources that compress return into 1814 or 1815 are not followed for the transfer date. The Dutch parliamentary overview is used selectively; its general statement of uninterrupted Dutch rule and oversimplified exchange-of-colonies account are not adopted.

Abolition in 1863 is separate from the end of compulsory state-supervised labour in 1873; the age qualification follows the archive guide rather than broad language applying the rule to every freed person. Autonomy in 1954 and sovereign independence in 1975 are different transitions. The post-1975 phase spans multiple governments and does not identify a current officeholder.

Some HTML pages supplied fuller indexed text than direct opening. The specific source passages were read, with access limitations recorded here. No inaccessible full book, untranslated object inscription or complete archival collection is claimed as inspected.
The narrative is author-checked against the cited passages and awaits independent historical review.

identityEvidence.assessment: The 1650 Surinam polygon is a coastal subset within the area of Suriname. The 1878 Dutch Guiana and 1914 Suriname outlines have almost identical extents. They support a shared geographic narrative, not a claim of unchanging sovereignty or complete colonial control over the interior. The adjacent guiana and british-guiana outlines are broader and are not attached to this card. All geometry remains unchanged and unverified.
